newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Sintercast signs deal in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Sintercast signs deal in Mexico.

text.p: Swedish development company Sintercast, embroiled in the Morgan Grenfell fund inquiry, on Friday announced an agreement with a North American foundry over its technology for casting car engine blocks.
In a joint statement Sintercast and Cifunsa, a subsidiary of Grupo Industrial Saltillo, announced a contract for the Swedish company to install its system at a plant in Saltillo, Mexico.

This is to develop high-volume production of Compacted Graphite Iron automotive and diesel components, mainly engine blocks and cylinder heads basically for the North American and European market, the statement said.
Sintercast's chief executive officer, Bertil Hagman, said the agreement with Cifunsa was an important milestone for his company that had not reported any significant sales to date.
"This confirms that Sintercast Compacted Graphite Iron (CGI) is now a competitive material for automotive components," he said in the statement.

He described CGI as an intermediate form of cast iron with substantially higher strength, stiffness and wear resistance than grey iron which provides new opportunities to save weight, reduce noise, vibration, harshness and increase performance.
Sintercast shares have soared on the Swedish bourse in recent years, rocketing to 550 crowns this summer. It was viewed as a highly speculative stock.
Since it was revealed that up to 57 percent of the companies shares could be owned by one of the three Morgan Grenfell investment funds currently under investigation, the share price has plummeted.
Sintercast shares were untraded at 255 crowns on Friday.
